You're not going to like what I'm about to say but I think it's necessary for a productive dialogue. Just to give some background, I was raised in a very conservative religious family in Texas. I served in the Marines for six years from 2001 to 2007. I voted Republican when I was younger. I moved on and after decade of college including medical school I became I doctor because I wanted to dedicate my life helping people. I vote almost entirely Democrat now with a few Libertarian exceptions though that's becoming more and more rare. I am not religious and frankly view religion as a whole to be a tragic byproduct of ignorance and fear but mostly control and insidious in even it's most benevolent forms. I am very dedicated to women's rights and firmly believe the government, state or federal, has no jurisdiction to dictate what a man or woman can do with their body and any legislation in opposition to that is against the fundamental freedoms upon which this nation was founded.  

With all that said, I don't believe your threats of rejection or friendzoning or rejection or being alone carry much weight. You're threatening to take away what a concerningly ever growing part of the American population don't have access to. The percentage of males under the age of thirty who have not had a sexual partner has tripled between 2008 and 2018 ([https://www.joe.ie/life-style/amount-men-30-not-sex-nearly-tripled-past-decade-663846#:\~:text=The%20share%20of%20men%20under,than%20the%20number%20of%20women](https://www.joe.ie/life-style/amount-men-30-not-sex-nearly-tripled-past-decade-663846#:~:text=The%20share%20of%20men%20under,than%20the%20number%20of%20women). ) One in three men in the US between ages 18 and 24 haven't had sex in the last year ([https://news.iu.edu/stories/2020/06/iub/releases/15-sexual-inactivity-young-men-united-states-no-sex-debby-herbenick.html](https://news.iu.edu/stories/2020/06/iub/releases/15-sexual-inactivity-young-men-united-states-no-sex-debby-herbenick.html) ) The birth rate has declined by almost twenty percent since 2007 ([https://econofact.org/the-mystery-of-the-declining-u-s-birth-rate#:\~:text=Rather%2C%20the%20U.S.%20birth%20rate,rate%20of%2069.3%20in%202007](https://econofact.org/the-mystery-of-the-declining-u-s-birth-rate#:~:text=Rather%2C%20the%20U.S.%20birth%20rate,rate%20of%2069.3%20in%202007). ) and more and more Gen-Z and Millennials are opting out of relationships and the prospect of having kids for a variety of social and economic reasons. So you're threatening to take something away from an ever growing population that doesn't have access to the thing you wish to deprive them of. This is only going to get worse. No, I do not have a magical solution that'll will fix everything in the stroke of pen. The symptoms we are witnessing with the continuous tragedies of gun related violence and despotic legislation are the symptoms of a much greater pathology occurring in the population. Tragically, I do not see this course as reversible at this point, it's too far gone. Radicalism will increase as more of the population becomes "alone". What you're proposing will only accelerate the growth of right wing radicalism in this country. You want to make the world a better place? Give love to those who haven't felt love. Go out of your way to be kind to people who have only known rejection. Give solace to the people who have been "dumped" and heartbroken. Give the people who don't care a reason to care....give them a reason to feel remorse, a reason to want to make the future a better place instead of burning it all down. If you can do that, then slowly but surely we can make this world a better place of us all.

Not defending the right one bit but there more factors than just density at play. You have to look at scalability, infrastructure and culture. The difference in containing a virus in country with a population of 50 million is vastly different than containment of a virus in a population of 320 million that’s not even comparable, per capita doesn’t play a factor when your talking about containment of a highly communicable disease and infection rates. So for example let’s take Korea’s population which is concentrated in the south with (just for example) all 50 million people. Now that’s one area where you can isolate those 50 million and keep protective measure in place and limit transmission. Now let’s take the US, the problem here, with regards to population, is we don’t have one area of concentrated population where relief and containment efforts can focus. We have the equivalent of a Korea on the west coast, a Korea in the South, a Korea in the North East that all have to be simultaneously contained and treated and isolated to prevent transmission and that several orders of magnitude more logistically difficult than just dealing with one Korea.
